You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive. Unlike the conventional “Save page as”, `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share. If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available. ![Monolith GUI screenshot](assets/screenshots/gui.png) --------------------------------------------------- ## Installation | OS | Method | Instructions | | :--- | :---: | :--- `docker build -t y2z/monolith . && sudo install -b dist/run-in-container.sh /usr/local/bin/monolith` | | cross-platform | [Release artifacts](https://github.com/Y2Z/monolith/releases) | Every release contains pre-built binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux, as well as platforms with non-standard CPU architecture. | #### From [source](https://github.com/Y2Z/monolith) Dependencies: `cargo`
Install cargo (GNU/Linux) Check if cargo is installed ```console cargo -v ``` If cargo is not already installed, install and add it to your existing ```$PATH``` (paraphrasing the [official installation instructions](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/getting-started/installation.html)): ```console curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh . "$HOME/.cargo/env" ``` Proceed with installing from source:
```console git clone https://github.com/Y2Z/monolith.git cd monolith make install ``` Rendering pages in browsers (`-B`) comes as a feature that's on by default, builds that don't need it can be made smaller without it: ```console cargo install monolith --no-default-features --features cli ``` --------------------------------------------------- ## Usage ```console monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ ``` ```console monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html ``` ```console monolith https://some.site/ https://some.site/about https://some.site/contact ``` ```console monolith -F WARC https://some.site/ https://some.site/about -o some-site.warc ``` ```console cat some-site-page.html | monolith -Iifs -r audio,video -w frame,iframe -b https://some.site/ - -o - > some-site-page-with-assets.html ``` ```console monolith page-saved-by-browser.mhtml -o page.html ``` ```console monolith -a crawl.warc.gz https://some.site/ https://some.site/page ``` ```console monolith https://username:password@example.com -o example-basic-auth.html ``` ```console chromium \ --headless \ --window-size=1920,1080 \ --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw \ --virtual-time-budget=9000 \ --incognito \ --dump-dom \ https://github.com | monolith - -I -b https://github.com -o github.html ``` Results get saved into files named after the pages' titles. Several targets can be given at once: each one gets a file of its own, and links between them lead to those files, so that they can be browsed without going online. With `-F WARC` (or `WARCGZ`), all of them go into a single archive. --------------------------------------------------- ## Options - `-a`: Take everything from `archive` (WARC, HAR, MHTML, WebArchive) without going online, targets are URLs of pages in it - `-b`: Use `custom base URL` - `-B`: Let a browser render the page first (requires Firefox, or anything based on it or Chromium) - `-C`: Read cookies from `file` - `-d`: Forbid retrieving assets from specified `domain` - `-e`: Ignore network errors - `-E`: Save document using `custom encoding` - `-f`: Exclude web fonts - `-F`: Specify output `format`: `HTML` (default), `MHTML`, `WARC`, or `WARCGZ` - `-h`: Print usage information - `-i`: Remove all images - `-I`: Isolate the document - `-j`: Remove all scripts - `-k`: Accept invalid X.509 (TLS) certificates - `-n`: Extract contents of NOSCRIPT elements - `-o`: Write output to `file` (use “-” for STDOUT) - `-q`: Be quiet - `-r`: Completely remove `element(s)` from the document - `-s`: Exclude styles - `-S`: Save a simplified version of the page, like the reader mode of a web browser - `-t`: Adjust `network request timeout` - `-u`: Use `custom User-Agent` - `-w`: Wipe `element(s)` from the document, emptying their contents or sources, but preserving the node - `-W`: Only retrieve assets from domains specified with `-d` (whitelist) - `-V`: Print version number --------------------------------------------------- ## Content Security Policies Pages get saved the way browsers show them: what a page's Content Security Policy (from its response headers or its META elements) doesn't allow to be loaded or run gets left out. The policy goes along with the saved document, rewritten to allow what the document has been made of and nothing else, and what `-I`, `-j`, `-s`, `-f`, and `-i` keep the document from doing goes into it too. --------------------------------------------------- ## Blacklisting and whitelisting domains Option `-d` forbids retrieving assets from the specified domains, and adding `-W` flips it to allow only those domains, e.g.: ```console monolith -I -d .googleusercontent.com -d googleanalytics.com -d .google.com https://example.com -o example-no-ads.html ``` ```console monolith -I -W -d example.com -d www.example.com https://example.com -o example-only.html ``` --------------------------------------------------- ## Dynamic content Monolith doesn't feature a JavaScript engine, but it can make use of the one inside of a browser that's already installed: option `-B` opens the page in a browser, waits for it to finish rendering, and saves what the page has become, e.g.: ```console monolith -B https://example.com -o example.html ``` The browser runs without a window, from a clean temporary profile which gets deleted afterwards. It never gets access to your own profile, cookies, or history, gets only those cookies that were passed in using `-C`, and sticks to the same rules as the rest of Monolith: domains forbidden with `-d` and whatever got excluded with `-i`, `-f`, or `-s` don't get requested by the browser either. It identifies itself as what it is, unless told otherwise with `-u`. Firefox gets used if it's installed. Set `MONOLITH_BROWSER` to the browser's path to choose another one: anything based on Firefox or Chromium works, such as LibreWolf, GNU IceCat, Chrome, Brave, or Edge. The browser follows your system's light or dark mode, so pages that adapt to it get saved the way you'd see them. Set `MONOLITH_BROWSER_COLOR_SCHEME` to `dark`, `light`, or `auto` to choose for yourself. The browser pretends to have a 1920x1080 viewport, set `MONOLITH_BROWSER_VIEWPORT` to change that, e.g. to `1280x720`. Pages only load what they think can be seen, and those that adapt to the size of the window get saved the way they look at that size. Pages get scrolled through before being saved, since a lot of them only load things as they come into view. Set `MONOLITH_BROWSER_SCROLL_LIMIT` to the number of screens to go through (30 by default, `0` turns it off), pages that never end stop there. Set `MONOLITH_BROWSER_DISABLE_JS` to `1` to keep the browser from running the page's JavaScript, frames included, so the page gets saved the way it was sent, before any scripts got to change it. That's separate from `-j`, which removes JavaScript from the saved document. If Monolith gets interrupted, it takes the browser and its temporary files down with it. Should the page turn out to be a challenge which doesn't solve itself, such as the ones used to tell people from bots, the browser reopens in a window and waits for you to solve it. The saved page keeps its JavaScript, along with the responses it has received, which get replayed to it without any network access: buttons, menus, and other things that only rely on the page's own code keep working, but anything that needs a server doesn't. A saved page only contains what it has loaded while being saved, so parts of web apps that were never opened won't be there. Scripts of the saved page get modified to make that work: they're told the page's original URL, and imports get pointed at what's stored inside of the document. Frames that get added by scripts show what they had without running anything, frames from other websites stay empty. They can't reach out to anything, their content security policy doesn't allow it, and `-b` doesn't apply to them. Add `-j` to save a frozen copy of what the browser had on screen instead; that's also what MHTML output and `-S` always do. The same is available to the GUI (“Render in browser”) and to programs using Monolith as a library, by setting `browser` in `MonolithOptions`. Apps that have a web view of their own, such as mobile ones, can use `create_monolithic_document_from_capture()` to save what it has loaded. --------------------------------------------------- ## Proxies Please set `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` environment variables. --------------------------------------------------- ### Apify Actor Usage You can run Monolith in the cloud without installation using the [Monolith Actor](https://apify.com/snshn/monolith?fpr=snshn) on [Apify](https://apify.com?fpr=snshn) free of charge. ``` bash echo '{"urls": ["https://news.ycombinator.com/"]}' | apify call -so snshn/monolith [{ "url": "https://news.ycombinator.com/", "status": "0", "kvsUrl": "https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores/of9xNgvpon4elPLbc/records/https___news.ycombinator.com_" }] ``` Read more about the [Monolith Actor](.actor/README.md), including how to use it via the Apify UI, API and CLI without installation. --------------------------------------------------- ## Contributing Please open an issue if something is wrong, that helps make this project better. --------------------------------------------------- ## Archives Besides documents, Monolith takes archives as targets, and never goes online to complete them: whatever isn't in there stays missing. - WARC (`.warc`, `.warc.gz`) and HAR (`.har`) hold the responses a page has received. It gets saved along with its JavaScript and those responses, which get replayed to it the same way `-B` does it, unless scripts get removed with `-j`. They may hold many pages: the first one is what gets saved, unless the archive comes with `-a`, and URLs of pages in it are targets. HAR files have to be exported with contents. - MHTML (`.mhtml`, `.mht`) and WebArchive (`.webarchive`) hold a document with what it's made of. Its assets get embedded into it. With `-a`, archives are all there is to work with: targets are URLs of pages in them (each one gets a file of its own, linked to the others), and nothing comes from anywhere else. WARC archives given with `-a` more than once work as one, pages in one of them may have their assets in another. ## Testing `cargo test` runs unit tests first, then real browsers: one of each kind found, or whatever's listed in `MONOLITH_TEST_BROWSERS`. Tests that need them have nothing to do if there are none, set `MONOLITH_TEST_REQUIRE_BROWSERS` to make that a failure. ## License Monolith is free to use, copy, modify, and distribute, for any purpose, without even having to give credit: it comes under the [Zero-Clause BSD](LICENSE) license (0BSD).
